sections.heading: Planning your Lentor Gardens Residences interior
sections.text:
Lentor has been one of the more active north-Thomson clusters in recent years, with new homes and a retail podium already on our wider project file. Owners here often want a calm, residential interior rather than a show-flat: storage that can take family life, a living room that does not depend on loose cabinets, and bedrooms that are properly fitted. The carpentry that usually does that work is an entry cabinet, a living-room joinery wall, full-height wardrobes, and a fitted kitchen with a tall pantry. Where a common room is a study, a built-in desk is more useful than a table in the middle of the room. Maison is an interior designer; we specify built-in carpentry, not IKEA-style furniture, and we can work in both wide room views and closer material shots.

No official floor plan is on file, so typologies and room sizes are not published here. Thomson Reserve and AMO Residence sit in nearby District 20; those are internal links for readers, not a claim of a shared layout or a shared management handbook. We will not invent walking times to Lentor MRT or to Upper Thomson shops. Check your own stack, facing and the estate rules before you plan blinds, a window bench or a balcony cabinet.

After keys, inspect defects, measure, and obtain renovation approval before fabrication starts. A moderate carpentry scope is often planned at six to ten weeks on site after approvals, as an editorial planning allowance only. WhatsApp Maison with your approved plan and any key date you have in writing. We are not affiliated with the developer.
